candidates.above_next: a frame for the entire object model reaches further than a single typing discipline

also.why: one uniform rule replaces a hierarchy of special cases

beats.why: the sequence concept generalizes across a few types; first-class generalizes across all objects

harms: erases useful distinctions between kinds of value, so less can be caught statically
boxing everything in one object structure has a run-time cost
candidates.quote: One of my goals for Python was to make it so that all objects were "first class." By this, I meant that I wanted all objects that could be named in the language ... to have equal status.
candidates.statement: Every object that can be named has equal, first-class status: assignable, passable, storable, including types themselves.

strongest.why: treating every nameable thing as an object of equal status reorganizes the whole mental model of the language

candidates.above_next: the typing discipline shapes every line a programmer writes, where indentation shapes the surface

also.why: dropping compile-time checking is cast as corner-cutting that costs no eventual safety

beats.why: reassignable built-ins is one consequence of late binding, narrower than the whole typing model

harms: type errors surface only at run time, sometimes far from their cause
no compiler coercion, so passing an int for a float can pass silently (l75)
candidates.quote: In Python, variables are simply names that refer to objects. Variables do not need to be declared before they are assigned and they can even change type in the middle of a program.
candidates.statement: Variables are names referring to objects, needing no declaration, and all type checking happens at run time.

strongest.why: types live on values, not on variables, so a name is just a binding to an object; this rewires how one thinks about variables

candidates.above_next: indentation infects on sight, before code is even run, where a correctness policy shows only when something goes wrong

also.why: the layout you read is the layout the machine runs; no divergence allowed

beats.why: the colon only clarifies where a block begins; indentation carries the whole grouping

harms: whitespace becomes semantically load-bearing, so invisible characters change meaning
mixed tabs and spaces can break code silently
candidates.quote: instead of using braces for statement grouping, it uses indentation
candidates.statement: Statements are grouped by indentation rather than by braces or keywords.

strongest.why: removing braces makes the visible structure the actual structure, an economy that sticks on sight

candidates.above_next: a correctness stance outranks the explicitness convention that follows it

also.why: forbidding undefined result values reframes what a function may legitimately return

beats.why: not bothering users with implementation details is a comfort rule; never passing silently is a safety stance that bites harder

harms: forces handling or crashing where a caller might prefer a sentinel
exceptions used as control flow can hide costly paths
candidates.quote: I decided that there should be no undefined result values in Python – instead, exceptions should always be raised when no correct return value can be computed.
candidates.statement: There are no undefined result values: an exception is always raised when no correct value can be computed, and errors never pass silently.

strongest.why: a stand that a wrong answer is worse than a stopped program

candidates.above_next: explicitness as a named rule outranks the design-economy principle that comes next

also.why: a method is just a function; x.f(a) equals C.f(x, a), one rule with no special method syntax

beats.why: rejecting instance-variable declarations is the absence of a feature; explicit self is a positive rule seen everywhere

harms: every method carries a visible self, which users read as redundant boilerplate
ties the model to the function-with-first-argument equivalence
candidates.quote: With explicit references, there is no need to have a special syntax for method definitions nor do you have to worry about complicated semantics concerning variable lookup. Instead, one simply defines a function whose first argument corresponds to the instance, which by convention is named "self."
candidates.statement: A method is just a function whose first argument, by convention self, is the instance; explicit reference is the only way to reach instance variables.

strongest.why: making the instance an explicit argument is a stand for explicitness over hidden lookup magic

candidates.above_next: a design-method principle guides more choices than a single slicing convention

also.why: restraint about growing the language, keeping the surface small

beats.why: everything-is-a-statement is one instance of this restraint, not the rule itself

harms: reusing mechanisms can overload them past clarity (a class body runs arbitrary code)
avoiding syntax pushes complexity into conventions and __dunder__ names
candidates.quote: making the class object itself callable was the right, "minimal" solution, requiring no new syntax... what I had done was simply to turn each class into its own factory.
candidates.statement: Prefer the minimal solution that reuses existing mechanisms over adding new syntax.

strongest.why: solve by reusing what already exists rather than adding grammar, an economy of means

also.why: it reframes indices as boundaries between items rather than the items themselves

beats.why: the list comprehension's beauty is borrowed from set-builder notation; the slicing invariant is Python's own

harms: half-open intervals confuse newcomers who expect the last index included
0-based plus half-open is two conventions to internalize at once
candidates.quote: Using / 0-based indexing, half-open intervals, and suitable defaults (as Python / ended up having), they are beautiful: a[:n] and a[i:i+n]
candidates.statement: Index from 0 with half-open intervals and suitable defaults, so common slices need no +1/-1 corrections.

strongest.why: the adjacency invariant, one slice's end being the next one's start, is a small beauty that lodges in the head
